clue.text: It snarls up speech for one struggling to proceed

explanation.surface: Someone tangled up in their words, struggling to get a sentence out.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrambler is a device that garbles telephone speech, and also anyone clambering awkwardly forward over rough ground.

clue.text: Rope-worker's song in, for example, Irish hut

parts.note: the Irish is one example of a sea
a shanty is a rough hut, from an Irish word

explanation.surface: A sailor sings about an Irish cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish' looks like a nationality describing the hut but, with 'for example', it is the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shanty is a work song sung by sailors hauling ropes.

clue.text: Place to settle and develop roots

indicators.note: develop as in change form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A place to settle down and put down roots.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds settle for the night.

clue.text: You see some striking redheads here

definitions.text: You see some striking redheads here

parts.words: You see some striking redheads here
parts.note: striking as in struck to light, and the red heads are the tips of matchsticks in their small box

explanation.definitionFit: A small box holding matches, whose red tips strike against its side.

clue.text: Belgian vassal

parts.note: a man from the Belgian city of Liège looks like a feudal servant

explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman is a feudal vassal sworn to serve a lord; Liège is a Belgian city.

clue.text: Club to abandon evil ways

explanation.surface: A gentlemen's club urges a member to mend his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reform Club is a famous London gentlemen's club on Pall Mall.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reform Club is a London club; to reform is to give up wrongdoing and improve.

clue.text: Bill is part of a bird — it's taken for granted

indicators.note: the bill becomes part of the bird, sitting inside its letters

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
AC (account) is a bill

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher assumes the beak is simply one part of a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a beak, but it is the account abbreviation; 'is part of' puts it inside the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is understood or implied without being stated, so assumed.

clue.text: Insect dances round horse

indicators.note: the dances go round the horse, enclosing it

parts.note: trips are light steps, as in tripping the light fantastic
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: A bug dances around a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' means heroin here, whose slang abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrips are tiny winged pests that feed on plants, also called thunderflies.

clue.text: For a savoury dish, see note under Game

indicators.note: in a down clue the note goes beneath the game

parts.note: croquet, the lawn game played with mallets and hoops
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A menu note says to look under the game section for a savoury dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' suggests meat on a menu but is the lawn game croquet.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a fried roll of minced food coated in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Flower made from cloth

explanation.surface: A flower fashioned out of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword trick for a river, something that flows; the Tweed runs along the Scotland–England border.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river of the Scottish Borders, and tweed is a rough woollen fabric.

clue.text: Messenger finds a way to interrupt staff

indicators.note: the way breaks into the middle of the staff, splitting it

parts.note: a pole is a staff or stick
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A courier finds a route that cuts through the office staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees but is a stick; 'to interrupt' puts the way inside it, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostles were sent out to spread the gospel, the Greek word meaning one sent forth.

clue.text: Abstained because of fatigue

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in 'jailed for theft'
bore taken as weariness or tedium, the thing that fatigues

explanation.surface: Someone didn't take part simply because they were too tired.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to refrain, so forbore means held back from acting.

clue.text: Pull up with a jerk for unexpected obstacle

explanation.surface: A driver yanks the car to a stop at a sudden barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch trousers is to tug them up abruptly; a hitch is also a snag or difficulty.

clue.text: Poet's book and pen

parts.note: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament
a pound is an enclosure for animals, a pen

explanation.surface: A poet owns a book and a pen to write with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is an animal enclosure; 'Poet's' means 'the poet is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The American modernist author of the Cantos, a famous twentieth-century versifier.

clue.text: Poor Antonia, tail-ender in the steeple-chase

indicators.note: poor in the sense of badly made, so the name's letters are put in a new order
the ender of the word tail is its final letter

explanation.surface: Unlucky Antonia finishes last in a horse race over fences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail-ender' sounds like the last-placed runner, but 'ender' takes the final letter of 'tail'. The Grand National is Britain's most famous steeplechase, run at Aintree.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grand National, often just called the National, is the famous English jump race at Aintree.

clue.text: It contains breakfast food from the health bar

parts.note: drinking someone's health is a toast
a rack is a frame of bars

explanation.surface: Something sold at a health food bar contains breakfast food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'health bar' suggests a snack, but split it: a toast is drunk to someone's health, and a rack is a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast rack is a stand that holds slices of grilled bread upright at breakfast.

clue.text: Stay in period

explanation.surface: Someone remains indoors for a spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A stop is a stay or halt, and a full stop is the punctuation mark called a period.

clue.text: Favourite uncle perhaps possesses a bad temper

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: the rearranged uncle holds the a within it
perhaps signals that the word uncle may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A favourite uncle may have a nasty temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges UNCLE to ULNCE, and 'possesses' puts A inside it to give ULANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is sulky ill humour, a peevish mood.

clue.text: Fairy dance held in linen cupboard

parts.note: Moth is one of Titania's fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A fairies' dance is staged inside a linen cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes where the item is kept, not what it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Small camphor or naphthalene pellets are stored with linen to repel clothes-eating insects.

clue.text: They are associated with beer and cheese

definitions.text: They are associated with beer and cheese

parts.words: They are associated with beer and cheese
parts.note: the pub game of the phrase 'beer and', where the thrown disc is called a cheese

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'beer and skittles' means pleasure, and in skittles a cheese is the heavy disc thrown at the pins.

clue.text: Truly the dawn of romance in "Nineteen Eighty-four"

parts.note: yea is an old word for indeed or truly

indicators.note: the dawn of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: There really is the start of a love story in Orwell's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest Orwell's novel, but the definition is just the date as a number of the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: 1984 is a twelve-month span of the calendar, as well as Orwell's title.

clue.text: Reserve a holiday — it makes reading easier

parts.note: to book is to reserve
a rest is a break or holiday

explanation.surface: Booking a break gives time to catch up on some reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand that props open a volume so it can be read hands-free.

clue.text: Engineers in, say, a ship have a way to get out

indicators.note: the engineers sit in among the other pieces

parts.note: eg (for example) is signalled by say
SS is steamship, a ship
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers aboard a ship have an escape route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the engineers between the two halves of 'say, a ship'; Royal Engineers is the British Army's engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, the act or means of leaving.

clue.text: Some garlic at supper adds relish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A little garlic at the evening meal adds flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'adds relish' as the definition, but a noun is needed; 'adds' is a link and the definition is 'relish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is the old American spelling of ketchup, a tomato sauce or condiment.

clue.text: Car performance chart requires a signature

parts.note: auto is short for automobile, a car
a graph is a chart plotting performance

explanation.surface: Selling a car with its performance chart needs a signature on the paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An autograph is a person's handwritten name, especially one collected from a celebrity.

clue.text: A grill, initially on low, is now red

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word grill

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grill set on low begins to glow red.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglow means glowing, as embers do when hot and red.

clue.text: Pound bill — it's remitted in foreign currency

indicators.note: remitted taken as sent back, so the whole string is read in reverse

parts.note: L stands for pound, from the Latin libra
AC (account) is a bill
the word it, with 's as a link meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A bill in pounds is paid abroad in another currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remitted' suggests paying money but means sent back: L, AC and IT together are read backwards. The tical was an old Thai currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The tical was formerly the monetary unit of Siam, now Thailand.

clue.text: Dog caught by several soldiers

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
OR is other ranks, the army's rank-and-file soldiers
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A dog is captured by a squad of troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a short-legged Welsh herding breed favoured by the late Queen.

clue.text: Footgear for the lazy

explanation.surface: Slip-on shoes for idle people.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafers are slip-on casual shoes, and also idlers who loaf about.

clue.text: To be sick. English boy causes flap on plane

parts.note: to ail is to be ill
Ron, a boy's name

explanation.surface: A boy becomes airsick, causing a flap on the flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' suggests panic but is a hinged surface on the wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged surface on an aircraft wing used to control roll.

clue.text: It's the annual holidays — see the waves from the ships

explanation.surface: On holiday at the seaside, watching ships churn the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Wakes Weeks were the annual holiday weeks in the mill towns of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wakes Week was the traditional shutdown holiday in northern towns; wakes are also the trails of disturbed water left behind vessels.

clue.text: Fences come to a point in the country

parts.note: pales are fence stakes, or fences
a tine is a prong or point, as of a fork

explanation.surface: Fences converge to a point somewhere in rural land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like countryside but is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestine is the historic land and territory in the Middle East.
